extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, researchers, museum conservators, engineers, medical practitioners and science educators
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating and preparing short scholarly content for a scientific journal issue (book reviews, letters, reports, and practical notes) with attention to editorial, methodological and professional standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of restoration
rubrics_metrics.description: “This difficulty can be overcome by taking photographs of the picture before repair, so as to put on record what is the work of the master and what is the work of the restorer.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photograph artworks before any restoration so the original work vs restorer's additions are recorded for aesthetic and scholarly accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and supervision of cleaning
rubrics_metrics.description: “No important public picture should be cleaned until it has been authorised by a committee of experts ... the cleaner himself should be present and explain exactly what he is going to do, while everything he does should be under the direct supervision of the head of the Public Gallery.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require committee approval for cleaning important public works; the cleaner must be present to explain procedures and perform work under the gallery head's direct supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved cleaning techniques and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested methods: where alcohol is used castor-oil should be laid on the surface with a soft brush, then a mixture of castor-oil and alcohol dabbed on with a soft brush and removed by diluting with turpentine and sopping up with a large dry brush; where alcohol is insufficient copaiba balsam emulsified with ammonia might be used; if any friction is applied use a soft rubber point; examine at every stage under a powerful magnifying glass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gentle, tested solvents and lubricants, soft brushes and rubber points, stage-wise magnified inspection; choose solvents only after assessing power and effect; avoid harsh friction and monitor continuously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: “Editor does not hold himself responsible for opinions expressed by his correspondents. Neither can he undertake to return, or to correspond with the writers of, rejected manuscripts intended for this or any other part of NATURE. No notice is taken of anonymous Communications.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should sign submissions, expect no correspondence on rejected manuscripts, and accept that opinions expressed are the correspondents' own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography and references completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that bibliographies are short and that references to abstracts/epitomes rather than original works and citations without date or locus (e.g. 'Nicolot, Bour, Monier-Vinard and Buguet, Le Paludisine' without date) are not helpful to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full, precise references (authors, title, date, publication locus); cite original works rather than abstracts or epitomes to enable verification and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Index quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that the index “bears evidence of having been compiled by some one unfamiliar with this class of work.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure indexes are compiled by someone knowledgeable in the subject area so they are usable and reflect the structure and terminology of the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of purpose and comprehensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint that a volume's brief preface makes 'it not clear what the object of the work is' and that the book 'consists, in fact, of a series of short essays dealing with general statements rather than with actual data'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the work’s objectives clearly in the preface/introduction; match scope to purpose and provide sufficient data and analysis rather than only general statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: “The aim of an inspector should be to ‘scrap’ as little work as possible, to detect faults in materials and workmanship at the earliest possible stage of manufacture, and to pass all sound work with the minimum delay.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspection systems should minimise waste, detect defects early, and avoid unnecessary holding up of sound products—organise to improve trust and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspector qualifications and temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on the importance of 'the kind of temperament, as well as the qualifications, required in inspectors and viewers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select inspectors with appropriate technical qualifications and temperament (judgement, impartiality, attention to detail) suited to inspection duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook concision, currency and balanced coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: For a clinical laboratory manual: should present methods 'in concise and accessible form'; criticism that 'there is much detail which could with advantage have been omitted', inclusion of 'inaccurate Tallquist hemoglobinometer' is inappropriate, 'nearly half the book is devoted to the examination of the blood, and the chapter on urine is comparatively brief', and 'the estimation of basal metabolism is not mentioned at all.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textbooks should be concise, include up-to-date and accurate methods, balance coverage across major topics proportionally, and include important omitted topics relevant to the scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and factual accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: On an astronomy text: 'misprints, misspellings, and other errata being numerous. Some of them are likely to cause serious misconceptions ... difficult to suppose that the proofs were read with any care.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure careful proofreading and fact-checking; correct numeric and factual errors before publication because they can cause serious misconceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum design principle for general science
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle: 'The preparatory values are incidental. The adjustment between general science and special science must be made by the latter building upon what foundation the former lays, rather than by any attempt to prescribe that certain materials shall be used for preparatory reasons.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design general-science curricula to build broad foundations; allow specialised courses to build on that foundation instead of forcing general courses to be narrowly vocational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental rigor and reporting (soil-acidity study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments used powdered precipitates of silica, ferric oxide and alumina; control treatments (e.g. shaking precipitate with KCl and testing extracts with indicators); report of accuracy 'within about 10 per cent'; note about apparatus modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use chemically pure materials, appropriate controls, quantify experimental accuracy, describe apparatus and any modifications, and explain assumptions rather than invoking ad hoc chemical transformations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spectroscopy experimental controls and apparatus considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Observations that 'water vapour in contact with films renders them insensitive', that drying films restores sensitivity; that A.C./D.C. currents can dissociate water; the condensed discharge can form compounds and fog films; and that in one experiment 'no attempt was made to eliminate mercury vapour.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control environmental and contamination factors (water vapor, mercury vapour), choose discharge conditions carefully, dry/prepare detection media appropriately, and report those conditions because they affect spectral results.
